Proven: with the Armature modifier disabled - exactly what the FBX exporter does, per its own tooltip 'Apply modifiers to mesh objects (except Armature ones)' - orders A and B produce BIT-IDENTICAL geometry, 0.00mm mean and max, both posed and at rest. Modifier order CANNOT affect the exported FBX. It affects only the viewport preview, and there the CURRENT order is better: measured against the real Unity result (geometry frozen at rest then skinned), Armature->Shrinkwrap->Locs_Generator is 16.3mm mean off while Shrinkwrap->Locs_Generator->Armature is 69.0mm off and generates a different loc count. Reason: the Shrinkwrap targets Yemoja_Body, which is ALWAYS posed, so feeding it a rest-pose scalp smears it onto a posed skull. The general rule: when a modifier reads another posed object, its stack position does not decide correctness - the target's pose state does. Also note pose_position was 'REST', which is why this never surfaced.

182. HIDDEN IS NOT EXCLUDED FROM FBX EXPORT. Blender's exporter only skips hidden objects when 'Limit to -> Visible Objects' is ticked, and use_visible DEFAULTS TO FALSE. Worse, 'visible' means the EYE icon (object.visible_get()), NOT the camera/render icon - disabling something from renders does not hide it from export. This was found the hard way: a second live loc generator object, Yemoja_Locs with its own 117-node GN_Yemoja_Locs graph, was hidden and no-render but still evaluating to 18,868 triangles and carrying NO material slots. Deleted 2026-08-21 after confirming nothing referenced it. The legacy Hair mesh (9,029 tris, 34 bones) is KEPT DELIBERATELY as a fallback and MUST be excluded at export by ticking Visible Objects AND restricting Object Types to Mesh + Armature - the scene also holds 8 lights and _review_cam that would otherwise ship.

183. BLENDER RNA IDENTITY COMPARISON FAILS. `link.from_node is some_node` never matches - RNA returns a fresh wrapper on every access. Compare by `.name`, or use `in`/`==` which RNA implements properly. Peer of the existing 'node.parent is frame never matches' rule. Cost this session: a link-removal loop silently did nothing and reported success.

184. JOIN GEOMETRY'S GEOMETRY SOCKET IS MULTI-INPUT. Linking a new source does NOT replace an existing link, it stacks alongside it. Symptom is output geometry at exactly 2x. Always enumerate and remove the old links explicitly after rewiring a join.

185. REALIZE INSTANCES ON SLOTLESS INSTANCES PRODUCES A NULL MATERIAL SLOT BEFORE Set Material ever runs, and Set Material then APPENDS to it giving [NULL, mat]. Extends rule 176: set the material on the INSTANCE TEMPLATE, before instancing and realizing - not after.

186. Image.scale() DOES NOT RESIZE THE PIXEL BUFFER OF A FILE-BACKED IMAGE. The datablock reports the new size but assigning pixels raises 'array length cannot be changed'. Create a new image datablock at the target size instead.
187. FunctionNodeRandomValue IN 5.2 EXPOSES ONLY FOUR SOCKETS for data_type FLOAT: Min(0), Max(1), ID(2, INT), Seed(3, INT). Index 2 is NOT a float. Set by name, never by index.
188. EEVEE'S ENGINE ENUM IN THIS BUILD IS 'BLENDER_EEVEE', not 'BLENDER_EEVEE_NEXT'. Valid values are ('BLENDER_EEVEE','BLENDER_WORKBENCH','CYCLES').

189. DETAIL TEXEL DENSITY, NOT TEXTURE RESOLUTION, IS THE BINDING CONSTRAINT ON FIBRE REALISM. Measure texels per mm AROUND the strand and ALONG it separately. Nyquist means the finest representable feature is two texels. The locs sat at 2.88/mm around and 1.24/mm along, i.e. a 1.61mm floor, which is why every fibre map read as broad soft grooves no matter how good its content.

190. THE SCALP BASE SHARES UV0 WITH THE LOC TUBES. Measuring 'tube u range' without excluding it returns the BODY ATLAS range (0.267), not the tube's real span (0.0195). Partition by material index or by an attribute before measuring any UV extent on Yemoja_Scalp.

191. TIP CARDS NOW LIVE IN NEGATIVE u (-1.00 to -0.30), leaving the entire positive u axis free for per-strand offsets. is_card is a shader test, u < -0.1. The Curl Map node undoes the u remap; it no longer remaps v.

192. root_fade AND is_card ARE RETIRED AS FLOAT ATTRIBUTES. Root fade = UV.y / 0.2913 (verified identical to 3.4e-8 across 5,244 loops); card selection = negative u. Neither needs an export channel, because UVs always survive FBX.

193. PER-STRAND VARIATION USES A GOLDEN-RATIO GRID INDEX, NOT A SINE HASH. Roots sit on a regular lattice, so sin-based hashes clump badly (33 of 46 gaps within 0.02). idx = round(u*12) + round(v*10)*12 then frac(idx * 0.6180339887) gives max deviation 0.044 from uniform, all distinct.

194. FOR A HEIGHT FIELD, HORIZON-BASED AO IS RAY-TRACED AO. A height field cannot have overhangs, so a high-to-low geometry bake and horizon sampling of the height compute the same quantity. Compute it directly (16 directions x 14 steps, wraparound so it tiles) - about a second, versus a fragile bake setup.

195. NORMAL-MAP STRENGTH MUST BE SOLVED AGAINST A MEASURED MEAN DEVIATION, never guessed. Bisect the height amplitude until mean normal deviation hits target (30 degrees reads as fibre). Guessing produced 75 degrees once and 54 degrees once, both of which read as noise rather than surface.

196. A NORMAL MAP THAT WAS AUTHORED RATHER THAN DERIVED FROM HEIGHT IS NOT EXACTLY INTEGRABLE. Poisson recovery of a height field from Yemoja_Fuzz_CoilNormal_v3_wisp correlated only 0.655 with the source slopes, because the map carries rotational components no height field can produce. Normals are still exact when used directly; only derived AO/roughness are approximate.

197. A TILING DETAIL MAP MUST BE PERIODIC IN BOTH AXES. Requires integer shears, fibre periods that divide the texture size, index-based (not coordinate-based) hashes, and wrap-mode blur. Verify by comparing the wrap-seam difference against the interior gradient - equal means seamless.

198. CYCLES OVERSTATES HAIR AO. Four area lights plus global illumination find every crevice; URP on mobile has one directional light and no bounce. Judge hair material in EEVEE, which is far closer to the shipping renderer. Every A/B in this project before 2026-08-22 was judged in Cycles.

199. PRINCIPLED HAIR BSDF, HAIR INFO, INTERCEPT AND PROCEDURAL NOISE NODES DO NOT EXIST IN URP AND DO NOT EXPORT. Any hair-shader advice built on them is Cycles-only. Portable equivalents: Intercept is our root_arclen; noise must be baked to a texture; radial roughness has no URP analogue at all. Very high roughness (0.82, i.e. URP smoothness 0.18) IS portable and is the single most valuable idea from that class of advice.

200. FRIZZ CARDS COST FILL RATE, NOT TRIANGLES. 540 alpha-tested quads is 1,080 tris - nothing - but alpha test disables the early-Z fast path on mobile tile GPUs, so overlapping transparent quads on the silhouette are the real cost. Enlarging a card is free in triangles and roughly linear in fragment cost.

201. IMAGE COLORSPACE MUST BE SET BEFORE THE PIXEL WRITE. Setting image.colorspace_settings.name AFTER pixels.foreach_set() writes pure black RGB to disk on save, while alpha writes correctly and the in-memory array still looks right. Order is: images.new -> set colorspace -> foreach_set -> update -> save. Use a byte buffer; float_buffer=True writes at the wrong gamma to 8-bit PNG (0.5 comes back as 0.214). Always verify by reloading from disk, never by reading back the array you just built.

202. AN OBJECT SOCKET ON A GEOMETRY NODES GROUP INPUT DOES REGISTER A DEPSGRAPH DEPENDENCY - CORRECTED 2026-08-23. It was originally recorded as broken, but that test was confounded: the Curves object still had a parent and used the emitter as its surface, either of which independently empties Object Info (see rule 203). With those cleared, an Object socket driven from the modifier panel works and SURVIVES A SAVE/RELOAD - verified. Panel pickers for cross-object references are therefore fine. If one ever comes back empty, suspect rule 203 first, not the socket.

203. A CURVES OBJECT USED AS A GUIDE SOURCE MUST HAVE NO PARENT AND MUST NOT USE THE EMITTER AS ITS data.surface, AND MUST STAY VISIBLE IN BOTH VIEWPORT AND RENDER. Each independently makes Object Info return empty geometry, and the symptom is always the same: the locs silently vanish and only the bare scalp renders. AMENDED 2026-08-23: the dependency is resolved when the depsgraph is BUILT, i.e. at file load - not when you change the setting. So binding surface to the emitter mid-session appears harmless and only breaks after the next load, and CLEARING it afterwards does NOT restore anything because no rebuild occurs. Recovery is to cycle the Object Info pointer through another object and back. THE FIX: bind data.surface to Yemoja_Body, never to the emitter (Yemoja_Scalp). Nothing reads the curves from the body, so there is no loop, the binding can stay permanently, and the sculpt brushes keep working. Verified across a save/reload on 2026-08-23. hide_set, hide_viewport, hide_render and the visible_camera ray flags all still remove it from the evaluated set - use a transparent material to stop the guide object rendering.

204. NEW GEOMETRY NODES INTERFACE SOCKETS ARRIVE ON THE MODIFIER AS 0 / FALSE / NONE, NOT AS THE INTERFACE DEFAULT. A freshly added socket reads as off even though the panel shows its default. Always write the intended value to the modifier explicitly after adding a socket.

205. A BOOLEAN FED INTO A DISTRIBUTE POINTS ON FACES 'SELECTION' INPUT DOES NOT GATE THE BRANCH. It evaluated identically on and off. Use an explicit geometry Switch node after the Realize instead - it also skips the instancing work entirely when off, so it is cheaper as well as correct.

206. WITH ALPHA CLIPPING, OPACITY FADES DO NOT SOFTEN ANYTHING. The threshold is binary, so a gradient only moves where the hard edge lands. Soft or frayed ends must come from the drawn SHAPE - taper strand width to zero and stagger where each strand starts and ends. This is why hair cards kept terminating in straight lines with sharp corners.

207. THE ARMATURE IS KEPT IN REST POSITION IN THIS FILE, SO ANY RIG TEST REPORTS ZERO MOVEMENT AND LOOKS LIKE FAILURE. Temporarily set armature.data.pose_position='POSE' to verify skinning, then set it back to 'REST'. Always test against a known-good control object (the brow cards) - a zero reading on the control is what reveals the test itself is broken.

208. A SQUARE TEXTURE ON A NON-SQUARE CARD FLATTENS CURVES INTO STRAIGHT RUNS WITH A CUSP WHERE THEY TURN. A round spiral cannot fit a 3.2:1 card at all. Either match the texture's aspect to the card's measured aspect so texels stay square, or design the drawn shape for the aspect you actually have. Measure the card by regressing vertex position against UV - do NOT assume u is the width axis, it is the LENGTH axis on the baby hair cards.

209. DETAIL NORMAL TILING ASPECT, NOT AMPLITUDE, DECIDES WHETHER A SURFACE READS AS FIBRE OR AS STONE. On-model feature elongation is (texture grain aniso) x (texels/mm across / texels/mm along). At ~2:1 the locs read as cast concrete; ~12:1 reads as combed fibre; ~20:1 starts to look like brushed metal. Fix the aspect ratio before touching Normal Map strength - measured deviation was already under the 30 degree target when the surface looked worst.

210. THE COMBED-GUIDE OBJECT'S MATERIAL RIDES INTO THE GENERATOR OUTPUT AS AN EMPTY SLOT. Object Info brings the Curves object's material with its geometry, and Set Material APPENDS rather than replaces (rule 176), so 'Yemoja_LocGuides_Invisible' now sits at material_index 0 on Yemoja_Scalp's evaluated mesh carrying ZERO polygons. 'Yemoja_Eye_mat' is empty the same way. Unity creates a submesh per material slot, so two empty slots become two wasted submeshes and two draw calls on export. Strip empty slots before FBX export and re-run the 'every submesh bound, 0 nulls' check. Verified 2026-08-23: polys per index = {1: 3220 hair, 2: 117 scalp}, indices 0 and 3 empty.

211. THE FUZZ ROOT VALUE IS A MANUAL TWIN OF THE LOCS' ROOT VALUE - KEEP THEM EQUAL BY HAND. 'RootVal_ramp' (Map Range) in Yemoja_Hair_mat darkens loc albedo toward the scalp via the root_arclen attribute; its To Min is the root multiplier. 'RIG_fuzz_rootval' (Value node) in Yemoja_Fuzz_mat must carry the SAME number, because the fuzz is the undergrowth the locs grow out of and any mismatch shows as a step at the hairline. Blender cannot link a value across two materials without a driver, so this follows the file's RIG_* Value-node convention instead. Current setting 0.75 in both (root albedo x0.75, i.e. 25% darker than the tips). Change one, change the other, then eyeball the hairline.

212. THE Mix NODE HAS FOUR INPUT SOCKETS ALL NAMED 'B' - NEVER SELECT THEM BY NAME. On ShaderNodeMix the inputs are 0 Factor(VALUE), 1 Factor(VECTOR), 2 A(VALUE), 3 B(VALUE), 4 A(VECTOR), 5 B(VECTOR), 6 A(RGBA), 7 B(RGBA), 8 A(ROTATION), 9 B(ROTATION). Code of the form [i for i in node.inputs if i.name=='B'][-1] silently grabs the ROTATION socket at index 9. This happened on 2026-08-28 and cost most of a session: the link LOOKED connected in the node graph, the shader compiled with no error, and the RGBA B socket silently fell back to its default flat 0.5 grey - which, with blend_type MULTIPLY and Factor 1.0, halved the entire hair albedo. Three consecutive A/B tests showed EXACTLY zero change and were wrongly read as aesthetic failures. Index RGBA sockets explicitly (inputs[6]/inputs[7], outputs[2]) and assert socket .type after wiring. General lesson: a change producing literally zero delta means broken plumbing, not a failed idea.

213. THE LOC MASK'S GREEN CHANNEL MULTIPLIES BASE COLOUR AND WAS THE REAL SOURCE OF THE 'GREY PATCHES'. Separate Color.Green -> Mix.B(RGBA) with blend MULTIPLY. In Yemoja_Hair_Mask_v2_fuzz.png that channel ran 0.384 (p5) to 0.937 (p95) with 46% of its energy at mid/blotch frequency, punching the albedo down by up to 60% in patches. Yemoja_Hair_Mask_v3_deblotch.png compresses it to 0.827-0.984 and leaves R (GlossBoost), B and A (Math.002 mix factor) byte-identical. Zero performance change: same 256x256, same single fetch. This was never a normal-map problem - the blotches survived every detail-normal swap unchanged, which is what pointed at the albedo path.

214. AO BAKED INTO THE MASK'S FREE BLUE CHANNEL WAS TESTED AND REJECTED ON AESTHETIC GROUNDS, NOT COST. Blue is unwired and free, and Yemoja_Hair_Mask_v4_ao.png (cavity reconstructed from the coil normal by Frankot-Chellappa integration) is on disk. Wired in, it reads as WOVEN CLOTH rather than hair - Stephanie rejected it 2026-08-28. Keep the locs bright. Blue remains available for anything else. Do not re-add AO without an A/B; the earlier 'AO does nothing' finding was an artifact of rule 212 and is not evidence either way.

215. MACRO INTERLOCKING PATTERNS IN THE DETAIL NORMAL DO NOT SURVIVE AT JUDGING DISTANCE. Four candidate 256x256 detail normals (chevron, helical wrap, cellular clump, jittered chevron) were rendered against the existing Yemoja_Fuzz_CoilNormal_v3_wisp at head-and-shoulders framing, which is the range Stephanie judges from. All read FLATTER and more plastic than the control, because the map is tiled 12.47 x 3.52 so macro features land on a handful of screen pixels and average to grey. What carries the hair at this range is the FINE VERTICAL FIBRE STREAKING. Rule 209 stands: feature ASPECT is the lever, not feature TYPE. Candidates are on disk as Yemoja_Hair_LocNormal_v*.png; do not re-litigate without changing tiling or resolution.

216. THE LOC UVs ARE ALREADY PERFECT AXIS-ALIGNED STRIPS - DO NOT 'FIX' THEM. Measured on the evaluated mesh: along-strand edges have dU of exactly 0, around-tube edges have dV of exactly 0. V runs down the strand, U runs around the tube. root_arclen spans 0 to 2.246 (median 0.969) on hair geometry. External advice to 'straighten the UV islands into vertical strips' has been checked and is already satisfied; acting on it would mean re-unwrapping correct geometry.

217. BLENDER'S BACKFACE CULLING DOES NOT EXPORT THROUGH FBX. use_backface_culling is Blender-only; the saving only lands when URP's Render Face is set per material in Unity. Table in README_unity_import.md section 4.

218. Yemoja_Hair_mat must be Render Face BOTH; Yemoja_Hair_Opaque_mat must be FRONT. Hair_mat carries the 184 single-sided tip-card triangles - set to Front they vanish for whichever fighter faces away. FaceOpponent ROTATES rather than mirroring scale, so winding is not the cause. General lesson: a culling measurement taken across combined geometry EXPIRES when a material split separates that geometry.

219. Anything whose appearance lives in the node graph or a colour attribute does NOT reach Unity (cf. rule 59, lips). Hair colour/alpha/gloss and fuzz alpha were baked to flat PBR maps 2026-08-30. Before adding any new node-driven look, decide how it will bake.

220. Blender's images live INSIDE Assets/CharacterModels/Yemoja/textures and are NOT packed. A texture Unity does not reference may still be referenced by the .blend - always exclude Blender-referenced files from Unity-side texture cleanup.

221. bpy.data.libraries.load(link=False) appends an object's DEPENDENCIES too - a Mirror modifier's mirror_object drags in the whole body and armature. Remove by diffing datablock lists before/after, never by removing only the names you asked for. This produced two duplicate rigs on 2026-08-30 (cf. the Armature.001 incident).

222. ALPHA CLIPPING CANNOT REPRODUCE A SOFT ALPHA GRADIENT. Fuzz alpha spans 0..1 but only 12.4% falls below 0.5, so clipping rendered solid quads. Soft fades need Surface Type Transparent. Check the alpha HISTOGRAM, not just its range, before choosing clip vs blend.

223. Blender's Decimate vertex group WEIGHTS collapse cost, it does not protect zero-weight vertices - 158 garment triangles were lost that way. To decimate a subset safely, separate it to its own object, decimate, then join back.

224. UNNORMALISED WEIGHTS ARE INVISIBLE IN BLENDER but not in Unity. Blender's armature normalises at deform time; Unity clamps to 4 influences FIRST then normalises. Yemoja_Clothes shipped 96 five-influence vertices this way. Normalise and limit to 4 before every export.

225. The rest mesh sat 0.14324 Blender units BELOW z=0 from at least v2 until 2026-08-30. That constant is what appeared as the -0.03 end of the 'toe clearance -0.03 to -0.39' note in every Unity import record, repeatedly misattributed to pose lean. Fixed by shifting all 18 root objects up; the Armature object now carries a Z translation of 0.14324 ON PURPOSE.
226. ALWAYS MEASURE THE NULL CASE. 82 clothing verts already sit inside the body at rest; without that control the forward lunge reads as a cloth failure when it is identical to standing still.

227. A TEXTURE CANNOT REPRESENT DETAIL FINER THAN ABOUT TWO OF ITS OWN TEXELS. The 2048 body atlas works out to roughly 1-2 mm per texel across Yemoja; a skin pore is 0.1-0.5 mm. Pores, leather grain and fabric weave therefore CANNOT be painted into the authored normal map at any level of effort - they sit below its Nyquist limit. The only mobile-affordable way to get them is a small map tiled many times (Unity: _DetailNormalMap). This is a physics limit, not a skill limit, and it binds Blender's 2048 map exactly as hard as Unity's.

228. URP TAKES DETAIL UV TILING FROM _DetailAlbedoMap_ST, NOT _DetailNormalMap_ST. Setting tiling on the detail NORMAL slot alone leaves detail sampling at 1x - a smeared blob instead of micro-surface - and logs nothing. Verified correct on Yemoja 2026-09-04: body (30,30) and clothes (14,14) on BOTH slots.

229. THE RUNNING BLENDER FILE IS THE AUTHORITY ON MATERIAL BINDINGS - ABOVE THIS MANIFEST, ABOVE README_unity_import.md, AND ABOVE FILE DATES. The v6 rule 'sort the texture folder by date and reconcile against the handoff doc' FAILED on 2026-09-04: a git operation had touched every texture in the folder to the same mtime, so date order carried no information at all. Read bpy.data.materials directly whenever Blender is reachable - which it now is from Cowork, via the remote-devices bridge, contrary to what claude/workflow-setup.md still says.

230. SEPARATE 'UNITY DISAGREES WITH BLENDER BECAUSE IT IS STALE' FROM 'UNITY DISAGREES BECAUSE THE TARGET RENDERER NEEDS SOMETHING DIFFERENT'. The first is a bug - the v6 Ocean2-instead-of-Ocean6 fault. The second is the job, and has two forms: TRANSLATION of what FBX cannot carry (hair node graph -> baked atlas, fuzz vertex colour -> baked map, use_backface_culling -> Render Face) and COMPENSATION for what URP lacks (no subsurface scattering; no procedural texture nodes, so micro-detail must become a tiling map). Never 'restore parity' by deleting compensation.

231. WHEN PROVENANCE IS UNDOCUMENTED, THE ASSET'S OWN PIXELS CARRY IT. Whether Yemoja_Hair_Baked_BaseColor_v2 was baked from the CURRENT hair graph was recorded nowhere - not here, not in either README. Settled two ways: (a) git log, the bake and Yemoja_Hair_BaseColor_v11_paler entered the repo in the same commit; (b) spectra, the bake's tube region (atlas u 0.5-0.947) correlates 0.86 with the v11 ramp and its tip-card region is teal-shifted, tracking Yemoja_Hair_CardAtlas_v3_tipTeal. Far cheaper than re-baking to find out.

232. BEFORE REMOVING A UNITY-SIDE ADDITION, MEASURE ITS FREQUENCY OVERLAP WITH THE AUTHORED MAP AND RENDER IT BOTH WAYS. On 2026-09-04 the two Detail_ normal maps were suspected of duplicating detail the authored maps now carry. Measured overlap of authored energy inside the detail band: 0.00% on skin, 6.51% on clothes - no duplication. Rendering them off reproduced the 2026-07-27 'her clothes don't look like clothes' fault exactly. A plausible-sounding hypothesis about a look is worth nothing until it is rendered.

233. AN ANIMATION FBX MUST DECLARE THE SAME REST POSE AS THE MESH FBX, OR HUMANOID RETARGETING SILENTLY MANGLES IT. Yemoja@Idle.fbx's bone node rotations differed from Yemoja_v7.fbx's by 20-121 deg. Unity derives each avatar's T-pose from the file it is built from and measures muscles relative to it, so the two avatars disagreed and the difference went into every frame. Measured: knees played at 0.6-6 deg where Blender had 20-27, both legs collapsed to near-identical straight sticks, and the trident read as held horizontally instead of upright. Nothing is logged. The giveaway is a clip that looks fine on OTHER characters.

234. TWO HUMANOID AVATARS IN A RETARGET MUST AGREE ON THEIR T-POSE, AND ON THEIR MUSCLE LIMITS IF EITHER IS NON-DEFAULT. Encode uses the source avatar, decode the target, so any difference in either is injected into the result. Making humanDescription.skeleton[] rotations identical on both sides took Yemoja's idle from 5.69 deg mean joint error to 0.035 deg. Limits matter only when they DIFFER: with both avatars widened and with both at default the result was identical to 2 decimal places. Never widen limits on one side only - and note Yemoja is driven by 9 animation FBXs, so 'both sides' means all of them.

235. UNITY DOES NOT CLAMP MUSCLE VALUES OUTSIDE -1..+1 - MEASURED, AFTER AN EARLIER VERSION OF THIS RULE CLAIMED THE OPPOSITE. Sweeping Left Forearm Twist In-Out on Yemoja's own avatar: 0 -> 0.5 -> 1.0 each rotate the palm exactly 76.40 deg, 1.0 -> 1.3 a further 45.85 deg (= 76.40 x 0.6, perfectly linear), 1.3 -> 2.0 a further 106.93 deg. So a curve reading 1.42 is applied in full, not flattened. CONSEQUENCE: do not widen HumanLimit ranges to 'fix' clamping that is not happening - it changes the normalisation on that avatar and desynchronises it from every other avatar in the retarget (rule 234). Out-of-range curves are a smell worth understanding, not a fault in themselves.

236. VERIFY A RETARGET WITH COORDINATE-FREE JOINT ANGLES - AND KNOW WHAT THAT METRIC IS BLIND TO. Blender is Z-up right-handed, Unity Y-up left-handed, so comparing raw rotations invites sign and axis errors. Comparing joint BEND angles plus limb directions as angles to three physically-defined axes (hips->neck, hip-to-hip, foot->toe) is invariant to both. BUT limb direction is completely blind to roll about the bone's own axis: Yemoja's idle measured 0.035 deg on that metric while her left palm was 48.6 deg wrong. For twist, measure something across the limb - the index-knuckle-to-pinky-knuckle vector works.

237. BLENDER'S FBX EXPORTER WRITES THE CURRENT POSE AS THE NODE TRANSFORMS, AND THERE IS NO SETTING THAT GIVES YOU BOTH REST NODES AND A LIVE ANIMATION. Measured on 2026-09-05 with two controlled exports of the same scene: with pose_position POSE the animation is alive (95 curves move) but the declared rest is 103.8 deg from the mesh FBX's; with pose_position REST the declared rest matches the mesh FBX EXACTLY (0.000 deg) and the animation is completely dead (0 curves move). At frame 110 the armature's rest-vs-posed deltas were ForeArm.L 120.8, Hips 27.1 - which is what the shipped file contained (121.4 / 27.3), confirming the mechanism. Therefore rule 233 CANNOT be fixed by export settings; it must be corrected on the Unity side after import.

238. AN UNCOMMITTED WORKING-TREE EDIT IS NOT A SAVED EDIT. This manifest was written to schema 48 on 2026-09-04, verified by reading it back, and was found reverted to schema 47 the next day - the reflog showed a concurrent Claude Code session doing 'pull origin main', a branch checkout, a commit and a fast-forward merge in between. TASKS.md survived; this file did not. After any durable write to the repo, verify it later rather than assuming, and get it committed rather than leaving it in the working tree.

eyeliner_decal.sheen_note: Roughness 0.15 barely reads in a static frame: the strip is near-flat so its normal hardly varies across 1-2mm and there is no angle range for a highlight to land in. On mobile with no reflection probe the sheen comes almost entirely off the main directional light, so the select-screen lighting rig decides whether it shows.

CRITICAL_skin_weight_fault.what: Yemoja_Body is skinned almost entirely to the .R bone set on BOTH halves of the body.
CRITICAL_skin_weight_fault.evidence: Total vertex weight .L = 13.25 vs .R = 4098.14. Only 2 of 23 .L groups carry any weight (Shoulder.L 0.44, UpLeg.L 12.81). Probed mirrored vertex pairs: world x +1.812 and -1.821 both report mixamorig:Hand.R at weight 0.939. Both thighs report UpLeg.R at 1.0.
CRITICAL_skin_weight_fault.scope: Yemoja_Body ONLY. Yemoja_Clothes is correctly sided (L 2159.05 / R 2082.04, 8 groups each side). Hair uses hair_loc bones and is unaffected.
CRITICAL_skin_weight_fault.already_in_unity: YES. The exported Yemoja_v2.fbx carries the identical fault (L 13.25 / R 4098.17). Not introduced by the 2026-08-12 sculpt.
CRITICAL_skin_weight_fault.why_nobody_noticed: Bind pose is correct and the idle is near-symmetric. Unity-side checks were avatar-level (isHuman, bone rotation, retarget) and do not test skin weights.
CRITICAL_skin_weight_fault.expected_symptom: On any non-symmetric animation the body's left arm and left leg follow the RIGHT bones, while the clothes on those limbs follow correctly - so the body and its garments visibly separate.
CRITICAL_skin_weight_fault.likely_cause: A mirror/symmetrize of weights that copied without flipping the .L/.R suffix. This naming-sensitive failure is exactly what the project-wide rename to Blender convention was meant to prevent.
CRITICAL_skin_weight_fault.fix: Re-mirror vertex groups on Yemoja_Body only, with proper L/R suffix flipping. Verify by re-summing total weight per side (should come out roughly balanced, as the clothes do) and by re-probing mirrored vertex pairs.
CRITICAL_skin_weight_fault.resolved_how: Rebuilt every +x (her left) vertex's weights from its local-space mirror partner on -x, flipping .L/.R on the way across. Chosen over a plain suffix rename because near-centreline verts legitimately blend both sides and a rename would collide on them; mirroring maps a partner's 0.5/0.2 to 0.2/0.5 correctly. 3264 verts rebuilt. The 133 centreline verts were left untouched - 18 of them already carried correct dual L/R weighting and were the only surviving legitimate .L weight.
CRITICAL_skin_weight_fault.resolved_verification: Totals now L 2056.68 / R 2054.74 (imbalance 1.94, better than the clothes' 77); 23 of 23 .L groups carry weight. Mirrored pair now reports DIFFERENT dominant bones - HandMiddle2.R at -x, HandMiddle2.L at +x, both 0.82. Per-vertex weight sums unchanged (min 1.0 / median 1.0 / max 3.0, same 226 non-normalised verts), proving weight was moved between groups and not recomputed, so deformation shape is untouched. Functional pose test: Arm.L moves 1457 verts on +x and 0 on -x; Arm.R the exact mirror. UpLeg L/R each move 695 own-side + 24 cross-side crotch blend.

hair_realism_investigation_2026_08_14.brief: Stephanie: 'I want her hair to look like real hair - work was done on the texture map a while back but not sure it reads well.' INVESTIGATED ONLY, NOTHING CHANGED. This is a scoped plan for the next modeller chat.
hair_realism_investigation_2026_08_14.current_setup: Yemoja_Hair_mat = flat Base Color (0.7137, 0.7325, 0.7476), CONSTANT Roughness 0.7012, Metallic 0, Alpha 1.0 (fully OPAQUE, no transparency), and ONE 1024 normal map (Yemoja_Hair_Normal.png, Non-Color). That is the whole material. Mesh: 4,622 verts / 4,391 faces / 9,029 tris, one UV layer, 45 hair bones, one material.
hair_realism_investigation_2026_08_14.FINDING_1_the_normal_map_is_good_but_ROT: This is the prime suspect and it is measured, not guessed. TWO independent tests agree the map has ONE dominant direction at about 45-60 deg in texture space: (a) slope-vector orientation histogram - 194,777 of ~262,000 strong pixels in the single 45-60 deg bin, peak ratio 8.9; (b) autocorrelation - correlation length 31 px along ~50 deg vs 5 px across, i.e. features are 6:1 ELONGATED, so these are genuine strands, not grain. MEANWHILE THE CARDS RUN AT 90 deg: median UV long-axis 90.1 deg, 3,136 of 4,314 quads inside 75-105 deg. So the strands in the texture cross the strands in the geometry at roughly 40 deg. That is what diagonal-scratch hair looks like.
hair_realism_investigation_2026_08_14.FINDING_2_it_is_NOT_a_blotch_map: Unlike the base colour and roughness maps that rules 67-69 correctly rejected, this normal map is genuinely high frequency: at a 128 px block split, 0.0% of variance is low frequency (R and G). Do NOT throw it away - it is good data pointed the wrong way.
hair_realism_investigation_2026_08_14.FINDING_3_roughness_is_uniform_RULE_88: Hair roughness is a CONSTANT 0.7012. Rule 88 was learned on the lips: uniform roughness reads as plastic. The identical fault is present on the hair and nobody has looked at it. Low-frequency breakup is the cheapest possible fix and, being scalar, is immune to rule 87 mirroring problems.
hair_realism_investigation_2026_08_14.FINDING_4_atlas_is_94_pct_empty: Hair occupies only 5.6% of its 1024 UV atlas (cards stacked, max 86 loops in one cell - normal for hair cards). Texel density along a card is 1.74 texels/mm median. If the map is ever regenerated, a small TILING strip would do the same job for a fraction of the texture memory - a mobile win in the spirit of rule 69.
RECOMMENDED_ORDER: 1. CHEAPEST, HIGHEST VALUE, TEXTURE-ONLY, NO RE-EXPORT: realign the normal map's strand direction to the card direction (~40 deg). CRITICAL: rotating a normal map is NOT just rotating pixels - the RG vector components must be rotated by the same angle or every slope points the wrong way. Alternatively regenerate the streaks procedurally aligned to +V, using the same technique as the leather-grain and skin-pore detail maps. Either way this needs Stephanie's eye, not a measurement, to confirm.

2. CHEAP, TEXTURE-ONLY: add low-frequency roughness breakup (rule 88). Costs one small greyscale map, or pack it alongside something existing. Uniform roughness is why it reads as plastic rather than hair.

3. MEDIUM: root-to-tip value gradient. Real hair is darker at the roots and the base colour is currently a flat constant. Cheapest route is a generated gradient map - note this does NOT violate rules 67-69, which are about not rescuing the MODELLER's flat-fill atlas, not about refusing to generate a good one.

4. PROBABLY OUT OF SCOPE FOR MOBILE: anisotropic specular. Real hair's highlight stretches along the strand; URP Lit has no anisotropy, so it needs a custom Shader Graph. Flag for the AAA copy, not this deliverable.
hair_realism_investigation_2026_08_14.DO_NOT_DO_alpha_cards: Do NOT add alpha-tested wispy tips to make the silhouette softer. The hair is currently fully OPAQUE and its silhouette comes from geometry. Alpha means overdraw, and per this project's own note overdraw - not vertex count - is a binding mobile constraint. Keep this for the AAA copy.

Root darkening and per-clump colour variation could ride on vertex colours at ZERO texture cost. CAVEAT that kills it for now: URP Lit ignores vertex colour, so Cowork would have to build a Shader Graph variant. Do not promise this without checking with him first.

blender_task_queue.why: Unity has carried a tiling detail-normal layer on skin and clothes since 2026-07-27; Blender has never had one. Consequence: the Blender viewport renders both surfaces flatter than what ships, so any surface-finish judgement made in Blender is being made against the wrong image - and every Unity importer who diffs the two materials sees a difference that LOOKS like drift and is tempted to 'fix' it by deleting the Unity layer. blender_task_queue.the_constraint_that_makes_this_necessary: Rule 227. The 2048 authored atlas is ~1-2 mm per texel over Yemoja; pores are 0.1-0.5 mm.
